deviations: loops_store/mod.rs register_geom_endpoint (Inner arm): the packet's Decision 3 step 3 unifies the fresh cut halves onto the canonical vertex by `change_vertex(&vl, &gvx, emap)` and claims this 'cannot disturb cross-store identity'. When the cut edge is referenced from more than one wire of the same store (the crossing_edges fixture cuts edge02/edge12, which each face pair shares across the two faces of one shell), the halves have strong_count 2, so change_vertex does NOT evict their ids from the shared emap (`if edge.count() == 1` is false), and those ids -- raw Arc addresses -- are left as stale keys pointing at this store's replacement. The allocator then reuses the very same addresses for the other store's fresh halves, `emap.entry(id).or_insert_with` hands them the stale replacement (which carries this store's boundary vertices), and the two stores' copies of the intersection edge diverge or reference the wrong shell's corners. The packet's design is unfaithful to baseline exactly here, so I added `emap.remove(&half0_id); emap.remove(&half1_id);` after the unify: the halves are dropped by the sweep and never legitimately referenced again (vl exists nowhere else), so purging their keys is safe and restores the invariant that every registration reaches each endpoint exactly once at its final point.

loops_store/mod.rs: `search_polygon_vertex` is implemented on `LoopsStore<P, C>` as `search_polygon_vertex(&self, loops_index, pt)` rather than the packet's bare `search_polygon_vertex(&self, pt)` sketch, because the former `add_polygon_vertex` (which it splits) was a `LoopsStore` method taking `loops_index`; the packet's signature omitted the index. No public API moved.
disagreements: Decision 3 step 3 claim that the Inner unify 'cannot disturb cross-store identity': it can, via stale emap keys colliding with reused Arc addresses (see deviations). Baseline never had this because its cut halves directly reference the shared mutable vertex, so no unify creates-then-drops fresh edges inside a shared map. The packet's reconstruction, taken literally, is therefore not faithful to the baseline semantics it claims to restore; it needed the key-eviction fix.

Decision 5 'poly commits keep baseline's relative order': the packet's own concrete step order puts polyC1(front) before polyC0(back), whereas baseline interleaves per store (poly0-front, geom0-front, poly0-back, geom0-back, poly1-front, ...). I verified this is unobservable -- the two stores never share layout, every discovery reads its store in exactly the state baseline read it (per-store commit order is preserved), and the per-curve cache contents are identical at every use -- so it is a wording imprecision, not a spec gap.

Decision 5 step 6 'skip that store's registration only, exactly like baseline's `if let Some`': baseline's geom add is guarded by the poly result (`if let Some`) but its projection/cut failures propagate through `?`, aborting the whole `create_loops_stores`; the packet's skip-on-None diverges there. Under the packet's semantics a projection failure would leave the poly store cut applied while the geom store stays uncut (layout desync). This is unreachable in the required tests (a projection failure at baseline would abort the currently-green tests), so it is documented rather than changed.

notes: Attempt-1 residue is fully deleted (no gemap0b/gemap1b/gemap_store0/gv0_store0/gv1_store0, no post-hoc reconciliation change_vertex calls, no set_point/Mutex anywhere under vendor/truck/); the four baseline maps (pemap0, pemap1, gemap0, gemap1) are restored with baseline's sharing. add_geom_vertex was replaced by pure discover_geom_endpoint + a thin register_geom_endpoint registration fn taking the pre-built canonical vertex (the packet's 'your call' option); the poly commit half was kept as commit_polygon_vertex alongside pure search_polygon_vertex. Each non-closed curve now builds ONE canonical gv0/gv1 (p_canon = d1.effective_point if store-1 discovered, else d0.effective_point, else the polyline endpoint) and registers that instance in both stores through the shared maps, with the leader readback writing p_canon iff either side discovered. The new test intersection_edges_share_identity_across_stores (Decision 6) reuses the crossing_edges fixture wholesale (two parabola surfaces, two faces per shell) and asserts the SecondType (IntersectionCurve) edge-id sets of the two geom stores are equal plus that at least one endpoint Vertex id is shared; I verified it FAILS on attempt-1's code (per-store caches diverge: store0 {a, x}, store1 {a, y}) and passes on r2. Crossing_edges itself fails on attempt-1's reconstruction and passes 10/10 on r2; punched_cube -- the packet's acceptance criterion -- passes. One environment finding: the intersection-curve construction (construct_polylines in polyline_construction) iterates FxHashSet/HashMap, so the polylines' order/orientation varies run to run; baseline is robust to that (shared mutable vertex), and r2 is robust now too after the key-eviction fix. All three existing loops_store tests pass unchanged (no assertion weakened, none deleted, no #[ignore]). QUESTION.md deleted as instructed.
